subject: Token envelope & streaming SLA — action plan and perf demo
messages:
From: Jason Malik <jason@finlytics.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + performance asks from today's call

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a couple of concrete asks so we can move forward: 

- Business context: we will embed model-driven summaries into investor dashboards (high frequency reads, occasional long analysis requests).
- Target latency: interactive experience goal is p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 300ms for typical queries (input ~1k tokens, output ~400 tokens). For longer analysis flows we expect input up to 6k tokens and outputs up to ~2k tokens; those can be async but must stream partial results.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline traffic estimate 120 rps, burst capacity to 400 rps for end-of-day runs.
- Streaming: must support chunked/partial output with sub-200ms chunk cadence for UX smoothing.
- Failure modes / fallback: if long-window throughput causes >500ms p95 we want an automatic graceful fall‑back to a summarized prefix or a cheaper model.

Next steps we discussed: a short perf-qualification run using a representative query set, followed by a live perf demo with telemetry. Can you confirm:
  * whether you can hit the streaming chunk cadence we asked for;
  * if a 6k input + 2k output envelope is supported in a single request (or whether we need to chunk client-side);
  * a rough timeline and who from your side will run the perf harness.

I've attached the SLA summary we put together. Priya from Regulus is copied — they will be involved on integration.

Cheers,
Jason Malik
Head of Platform, FinLytics
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jason Malik <jason@finlytics.com>, Priya Shah <priya@regulushealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + performance asks from today's call

Thanks Jason — great recap and exactly what we needed. Short answers upfront and next steps below.

Short answers:
- Streaming cadence: yes, we can stream partial tokens down to ~150–200ms chunk cadence depending on model choice and sequence lengths; we will validate with your query shapes.
- Envelope support: we support up to 8k input + 4k output in hosted configurations with tuned quantization and batching; for the largest single-request envelopes we recommend an explicit perf run to validate p95 behavior.
- Perf run owner: I will run an initial qualification with our infra team and then coordinate a live demo with Eng (Rishi) and Perf (Ben).

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) You share 20 representative queries (mix of 1k/3k/6k inputs) and expected partial-output cadence — Priya can drop these in the Drive link.
2) We run an internal perf sweep (48–72 hours) on a dedicated pool and provide telemetry (latency histograms, token throughput, KV cache hit rate).
3) Live demo with you + integration team showing streaming behavior and fallback policy (~30–45 min).
4) Follow-up: decide on Dedicated vs Hosted (capacity + cost comparison).

I've attached a draft action-plan workbook with proposed dates. Can you confirm the 20 queries by Monday PST? If so we'll schedule the perf window for Tues–Thurs next week.

-Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Quick recap + performance asks from today's call

Internal notes / TL;DR for perf team — forwarding customer asks and the attached SLA. Please read the highlighted sections. Key bullets:
- Customer (FinLytics) needs interactive p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 300ms for typical 1k->400 token queries. They also need a supported envelope up to 6k input / 2k output for async flows and chunked streaming for UX.
- Traffic: baseline 120 rps, bursts to 400 rps. They asked for ~150–200ms chunk cadence when streaming.
- Acceptable fallback: automatic truncation/prefix summary or fallback to smaller model to keep UX within 400–500ms p95.

Requests for you both:
1) Can we set up a dedicated perf sweep next Tue–Thu on a 4-GPU dedicated pool? Start with both the default 32-bit path and a 4-bit quantized variant so we can compare latency and token throughput.
2) Ben — please draft a short runbook template (what we measure, telemetry, SLO comparison table, and pass/fail criteria). Rishi — can you confirm availability for a live demo Fri or early next week?

Attaching: finlytics_sla_requirements_v1.pdf, mcap-action-plan-draft.xlsx, call recording.

Thanks — Marissa
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick recap + performance asks from today's call

Got it — I'll own the live demo coordination and run validation for streaming cadence. Quick plan:
- Ben will spin the perf harness and run two sweeps: 1) 1k input / 400 output shapes at 120 rps steady state; 2) envelope test with 6k input / 2k output at low concurrency to characterize p95 tail. Each sweep will capture p50/p95/p99, token/sec, and chunk latency distribution.
- We'll run the default FP32 model path and a 4-bit quantized variant; include memory/kv-cache metrics so we can recommend caching policies.
- Fallback policy: recommend a prefix-summarize + model fallback at 350ms p95 threshold. We'll provide a sample snippet for the client to use for graceful degradation.
- Timeline: Ben starts the perf window Tue 2026-12-01 02:00 UTC for 48 hours; I can demo Fri, 2026-12-04 16:00 PST (propose slot to customer).

Action items assigned:
- Ben: runbook + perf deck + initial results by Thu EOD (2026-12-03).
- Marissa: secure sample queries and confirm demo slot with Jason/Priya.
- Me: prepare fallback snippet, cost delta estimate between hosted/dedicated, and a short playbook to hit chunk cadence at scale.

I'll post the run results and a short summary in the Drive link once available.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior PM, Performance & Serving, Redwood Inference
